tagline: Once Route 135, now a back road to Farmville.
intro: Green Bay Road runs about eleven miles north through the Prince Edward countryside, from US 360 at the crossroads of Green Bay to US 460 east of Farmville. It was a state highway once, taken into the state system in pieces between 1930 and 1932, numbered Route 135 in 1933 and dropped to a secondary road in 1945.
Around Green Bay, peach growing did well in the 1930s and 1940s, until the larger growers and changing methods took the trade away.

moments.title: Green Bay
moments.text: The crossroads sits on US 360 between Burkeville and Keysville, where a Norfolk and Western mainline and the Southern Railway both gave it rail access.

moments.title: Twin Lakes State Park
moments.text: Opened in 1950 as Prince Edward State Park for Negroes, after Maceo Martin's family was turned away from another park, it was Virginia's only pre-civil-rights state park for African Americans.
